purpose: Simplified combined combat evolution key art for four species
stages:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: actual production key-art sheet for four 2D game sprites, awaiting keyframe approval, not an animation preview.

Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the four overcomplicated combined creatures in combinations-keyposes.png. Redesign their neutral appearance to be much cleaner and more biologically coherent. Input image 2 is the SUPPORTING STYLE/IDENTITY reference: the individually approved attribute sprites in singles-contact.png. Preserve their charming species identities, proportions, mouthless faces with exactly two dark eyes, softly painted materials, crisp dark contours and original casual-game sprite style.

Produce ONE clean 2-by-2 key-art sheet, exactly four complete creatures, ONE NEUTRAL READY POSE EACH. Top left sprout bean, top right spore mushroom, bottom left pebble creature, bottom right water droplet creature. All face mostly forward with a slight rightward attack orientation. Equal cell sizes, consistent camera, comfortable generous spacing and complete silhouettes. Genuine transparent background. No labels, borders, diagrams, shadows, action effects, particles, or floating specks.

Critical art direction: the combined evolution should read as ONE BIG ORGAN that has acquired several functions. Retain the five attribute ideas through structural integration and small details, not five equally large accessories. Use a clear visual hierarchy: recognizable original body first, one main evolved structure second, sparse tiny details last. Broad quiet areas, restrained accents, clear eyes. Make it feel inevitable that this species evolved this way.

SPROUT BEAN: retain a plump pale cream bean and two tiny feet. ONE continuous, elegant green leaf mantle grows from its crown and curves around one side of the body. This same leaf is protective and slightly thick like natural armor; its outside rim has a subtly sharp cutting edge, and ONE tapered tip supplies the piercing function. A couple of normal small sprouts help identity. Keep the face largely uncovered.Do not add separate scythes, a second shield, a huge spear leaf, or a bouquet of nectar buds.

SPORE MUSHROOM: retain the small cream mushroom stalk/body with two eyes and two tiny feet beneath ONE coherent coral-red cap. A slim, organically layered cap rim gives protection; a restrained blue-teal band is integrated into that same rim. ONE pointed purple-tinged continuation of the cap's upper-right edge gives both a sharp cutting edge and a piercing tip.Preserve a broad calm coral cap surface. No stacked complete caps, separate fan shields, rainbow balloons, or multiple horns.

PEBBLE CREATURE: retain a warm beige faceted stone body, two dark eyes and two tiny stone feet. Keep most of the beige stone clearly visible. ONE main emerald-to-violet crystal outcrop is organically rooted into an upper shoulder: one broad sharp facet and one tapered continuation supply cutting and piercing as a single geological structure. Shallow blue and rose crystal inlays, small and sparse, suggest armor and shielding as part of the stone skin.Premium gem shading from the references. No complete jeweled ring around the face, no piles of five large differently colored crystals, no separate giant shield.

WATER DROPLET: retain one continuous clear cyan gel body and two dark eyes, with the original glossy water highlights. Use ONE slightly faceted, gently polygonal body with a somewhat thicker protective outer rim; this one contour expresses both armor and guard. ONE flowing upper-right fin tapers into a sharp tip, combining cutting and piercing.Keep the front surface calm and open. No second left horn, no crossed fins, no overlapping second polygon/body, no separate shield plate, no extra eyes or feet.

Draw complete clean surfaces, smooth closed outlines and readable small-scale shapes. Match the reference sprite rendering rather than changing to 3D toy renders, flat vector icons, pixel art, or realistic creatures. These actual drawings will be the source artwork for later part separation only AFTER user approval.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: actual 2D sprite production key-art sheet awaiting user approval.
Edit the attached FOUR-character key-art sheet with only these targeted simplifications. Preserve the transparent background, 2x2 arrangement, painting style, camera, lighting, scale and all species identities.

BOTTOM LEFT PEBBLE: simplify much further. Keep its existing beige faceted rock body, face and tiny feet. Remove the entire necklace/ring of blue, pink and amber crystals from the left side, lower sides and bottom outline. Give the rock a continuous clean beige outline along the left and lower half. Keep ONE compact emerald-to-violet crystal cluster rooted at the UPPER RIGHT SHOULDER: the existing main violet tapered crystal and two smaller emerald facets can function as one natural geological outcrop. All large crystals must be confined to that one shoulder. Body protection should read in the rock's own broad facets. A maximum of TWO very small blue/rose mineral inlays may sit FLUSH inside the stone surface near that shoulder; no protruding side tiles. Only ONE tiny amber bead may remain in the seam just below the main cluster. At least 80 percent of the visible central body must be calm beige stone. This is a clear body silhouette with one precious outcrop, not jewelry covering a creature.

BOTTOM RIGHT WATER: keep the existing cyan polygonal body, single upper-right fin, two eyes, and tiny attached edge beads. Remove the two foot-like lobes/highlight pads at the bottom so it ends in ONE continuous gently faceted gel outline. This species has no feet. Do not add extra fins or a shield plate.

TOP TWO CHARACTERS: preserve their existing appearance and neutral poses. Do not change the sprout bean or mushroom. No extra characters, labels, diagram marks, shadows or particles. Preserve genuine transparency, crisp clean edges, and complete uncropped subjects. This sheet is source artwork for a possible later rig; do not produce animation frames.
